$comment: Provenance for every file vendored under schemas/. PRREV-002, PR-REVIEW-SKILL-002 v2 §6.2. sha256 values here are cross-checked against schemas/MANIFEST.sha256 by scripts/check_vendored_schemas.sh — two independent records that must not drift apart.

upstream.standard: Static Analysis Results Interchange Format (SARIF) Version 2.1.0, OASIS Standard incorporating Approved Errata 01
upstream.two_source_agreement: byte-identical (cmp exit 0) between the OASIS published document and the oasis-tcs/sarif-spec git blob
upstream.modifications: none — byte-identical to both fetched sources
upstream.self_contained: every $ref in this file is a local JSON Pointer (#/definitions/...); no $ref resolves off-host

schemas.why_authored: The in-toto Attestation Framework ships NO JSON Schema for the Statement layer. Upstream normative artifacts are Markdown plus protobuf; a recursive listing of in-toto/attestation@main contains exactly two .json files, both npm manifests. Recording this file as 'vendored from upstream' would be a fabricated provenance claim, so it is recorded as authored here, derived from the sources below.

derived_from.role: normative — DigestSet algorithms and lowercase-hex encoding
normative — parsing rules (unrecognized fields MUST be ignored; extension fields permitted)
reference implementation — per-algorithm digest byte lengths, custom algorithms unconstrained

upstream.authoring_rule: Where the Markdown specification speaks, it wins. Where it is silent, the Go reference implementation fills the gap. Every application of that rule is listed under 'decisions'.

decisions.basis: markdown ('Each element MUST have digest set') + go-reference (ErrDigestRequired)

markdown wins — statement.md says 'optional ... MAY be omitted'. The Go reference disagrees (ErrPredicateRequired); the normative Markdown is followed, and the divergence is recorded rather than silently resolved.

decisions.constraint: lowercase hex at the algorithm's exact byte length
decisions.basis: markdown ('lowercase hex-encoded values') for the case, go-reference (HexLength/digestLengths) for the length. Go's hex.DecodeString also accepts UPPERCASE; the Markdown's 'lowercase' wins, so an uppercase digest is rejected here and accepted by the Go reference. Deliberate: a receipt is byte-compared, and a case-variant digest breaks that.
go-reference — 'use of custom, unsupported algorithms is allowed and does not generate validation errors'
markdown parsing rules — consumers MUST ignore unrecognized fields; producers MAY add extension fields. additionalProperties:false here would reject conformant documents.

not_enforced: RFC 3986 s6.2.2.1 lowercase-AUTHORITY normalization on TypeURI. The scheme is enforced (^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:); the authority is not. A full RFC 3986 regex was judged more likely to produce a false RED than to catch a defect.
base64 well-formedness of ResourceDescriptor.content (typed string, contentEncoding annotation only — contentEncoding is non-validating in 2020-12).
Semantic agreement between a subject digest and the artifact it names. That is the guard's job (PRREV-003), not the schema's.

validator.network: required ONCE to install the validator; NEVER at gate time. scripts/check_vendored_schemas.sh proves the gate-time claim by re-running the full fixture table inside a network namespace with no interfaces (unshare -r -n) and an empty XDG_CACHE_HOME.
validator.regex_variant: default (ECMAScript via regress) — the patterns in in-toto-statement-v1.json are ECMA-262 compatible
